newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish 1996 terms of trade weaken two pct pts.
newsitem.headline: Finnish 1996 terms of trade weaken two pct pts.

text.p: Finland's terms of trade weakened by two percentage points last year, the National Customs Board (NCB) said on Tuesday.
Import prices rose 2.1 percent year-on-year in 1996 while export prices rose 0.2 percent.
"Due to the slight rise in import prices, the terms of trade ... weakened two percentage points on the previous year," it said.
The terms of trade rose in 1995 and hit a six-year peak in the first quarter of 1996, but fell through the rest of last year to end near the levels of Q4, 1994.
"Export prices were at a clearly higher level in the first half of the year," NCB said, referring to 1996.
The rise in import prices was mainly due to more expensive crude oil and petroleum products, it said.
Export prices of pulp fell 36.8 percent year-on-year in 1996, paper export prices fell 2.6 percent and paperboard export prices fell 4.0 percent.
Sawn goods export prices fell 7.6 percent.
Base metals export prices fell 11.5 percent last year while export prices of metal products and machinery rose 8.0 percent.
Chemicals export prices rose 2.9 percent, foodstuffs export prices rose 5.2 percent and in the category other industry, export prices rose 6.1 percent, NCB said.

Import prices of raw materials and production necessities rose 1.7 percent and liquid fuels import prices rose 22.8 percent while import prices of machinery and equipment for investment purposes fell 1.6 percent. @

Import prices of consumer goods rose 3.6 percent with foodstuffs, tobacco and beverages up 5.7 percent. Private car import prices rose 2.3 percent and other durable goods import prices rose 4.1 percent, NCB said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
